chats.answer:
For a laptop screen extender that works with just one USB-C cable, I'd prioritize three things:

True single-cable operation: One USB-C connection carries both video and power, with no extra power adapter.

No drivers required: Ideally, plug it in and your laptop recognizes the additional display immediately.

Portability: Lightweight enough to travel with, without putting excessive weight on your laptop's screen.

One important distinction: some extenders advertise “single-cable” connectivity but require a second cable for certain laptops or configurations. Others need DisplayLink software.

chats.answer:
For a laptop screen extender that works with just one USB-C cable, I'd prioritize models that carry both video and power through that cable, without needing an extra HDMI connection or power adapter.

There are two main types:

Dual-screen extenders: Attach to your laptop and give you two additional screens. Best for a portable three-monitor setup.

Single-screen extenders: Add one screen, typically with better portability, less weight, and fewer compatibility issues.

The important distinction is that USB-C connectivity doesn't automatically mean one-cable operation. Some products require two USB-C connections or an external power source, especially dual-screen models.
